applies_from.meaning: Chapter III, Sections 1, 2 and 3, except Article 6(5), apply from this date as regards AI systems classified as high-risk pursuant to Article 6(2) and Annex III; Article 27 is in Chapter III, Section 3
applies_from.source: Article 113, third paragraph, point (c)(i), of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 (OJ L, 2026/1744, 24.7.2026)

fria.note: This block decides only whether the Article 27(1) FRIA obligation applies to the deployer. Conducting the assessment itself (the content elements of Article 27(1) points (a) to (f) and the Article 27(5) template) is out of scope here.
rationale: the risk classification is not settled; Article 27(1) applies only to high-risk AI systems referred to in Article 6(2), so FRIA applicability cannot be decided yet

rule undetermined: no rule fired but prohibition-relevant (Article 5) and Annex III high-risk (Article 6(2)) flags are unknown, so the classification cannot be settled deterministically; the named facts must be provided before a minimal verdict is safe

features.description: SpamGuard is a machine-learning email filter deployed by a 20-person company for its own shared inboxes. It classifies incoming email as ham, spam, or phishing using message text and metadata, moves likely spam to a retrievable quarantine folder, and flags suspected phishing links for the IT admin. It never blocks, deletes, or answers mail on its own; employees read their own mail and know the filter exists.
purposes: classify incoming email as ham, spam, or phishing
flag suspected phishing links for the IT admin
